title: Singapore Saved Apple $2.7 Billion in Taxes This Year
summary:
Apple paid more income tax in Ireland than in Singapore in fiscal 2026, but it saved more in Singapore.
Apple's annual report shows that the company paid $4.96 billion in cash income taxes in Ireland and $3.25 billion in Singapore.
Against the 21% U.S. federal corporate tax rate, Singapore lowered Apple's tax expense by $2.67 billion, about $100 million more than Ireland did.
Singapore's lower tax rate and incentives would have saved Apple $5.49 billion before other taxes and adjustments.
The Financial Times estimated that Apple booked up to $50 billion in pretax profit in Singapore in 2026.

title: Canada launches the Real-Time Rail, bringing 24/7 payment infrastructure to the national economy
summary:
OTTAWA, ON, November 9, 2026 – Payments Canada today announced the launch of Canada’s Real-Time Rail (RTR).
Built in Canada and designed to serve all Canadians, the RTR provides accessible payment infrastructure through existing banking and payment channels.
Sereena Boparai, Chief Revenue OfficerParamount Commerce"The Real-Time Rail is a significant step forward for the integrity and resilience of Canada's payment infrastructure.
I want to thank Payments Canada and Finance Canada for turning a sovereign real-time payments network into a reality.
As a public-purpose organization, we own and operate: Lynx, our high-value payment system; the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS), our retail batch payment system; and the Real-Time Rail (RTR), our new real-time payment system.
